A one-figure model report

Source: R/model_report.R
model_report.Rd

Assembles a compact, consistent overview of a fitted model in a single figure: the coefficient estimates, the predicted effect of a focal predictor, a residual panel and a normal Q-Q plot, with a subtitle of key fit statistics. It is a convenience wrapper that composes several depictr plots with arrange_plots(), and serves well for a rapid model review or a report appendix.

Usage

model_report(
  model,
  predictor = NULL,
  standardise = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  glm_panels = TRUE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A fitted lm or glm model.

predictor

Focal predictor for the effect panel, given as in effects_plot(). If NULL, the first numeric variable in the formula (or, failing that, the first variable) is used, so a model with log(rainfall) shows the effect of rainfall.

standardise

Whether the coefficient panel scales each continuous predictor's coefficient by that predictor's standard deviation, leaving factor and binary contrasts in the outcome's units, as described for standardise in coefficient_plot(). Defaults to TRUE, which keeps the panel readable in this compact overview when the slopes are on very different scales. Set FALSE for raw estimates.

title

Overall title.

subtitle

Overall subtitle. If NULL, a line of fit statistics (number of observations, R-squared and AIC) is used. For a glm, the R-squared is the deviance R-squared described in model_fit_table().

glm_panels

For a glm, whether to draw the binned-residual and quantile-residual panels (the default) instead of the classic lm panels. Ignored for an lm.

seed

Optional integer seed for the randomisation of discrete quantile residuals, for a reproducible Q-Q panel of a binomial or Poisson glm. The caller's random number stream is left as it was.

Value

A 'patchwork' object (printable like a ggplot2::ggplot).

Details

For an lm, the residual panel plots the residuals against the fitted values, and the Q-Q panel is qq_plot() of the standardised residuals. A glm gets the panels residual_diagnostics_plot() draws for it (glm_panels = TRUE). The residual panel is a binned_residual_plot() (Gelman & Hill, 2007). The Q-Q panel plots randomised quantile residuals (Dunn & Smyth, 1996), which are standard normal under a correctly specified model whatever the response family, so the band of qq_plot() applies to them. The standardised deviance residuals of a binary or count model are not expected to be normal, so even a correctly specified model can put many of them outside that band (about a third, in a simulated logistic model with 400 observations). The quantile residuals of a binomial or Poisson model are randomised, and even under a correct model a run of them occasionally leaves the pointwise band. A departure worth acting on persists when the panel is drawn again with another seed. For a family with no quantile residual here, such as a quasi-likelihood family, the Q-Q panel plots the deviance residuals and its axis says so.

References

Gelman A, Hill J (2007). Data analysis using regression and multilevel/hierarchical models. Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, UK. ISBN 978-0-521-68689-1. doi:10.1017/CBO9780511790942 .

Dunn PK, Smyth GK (1996). “Randomized quantile residuals.” Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 5(3), 236–244. doi:10.1080/10618600.1996.10474708 .

Examples

fit <- lm(yield ~ rainfall + fertiliser + soil_ph + treatment,
          data = crop_yield)
model_report(fit, title = "Crop-yield model")


# A logistic model gets binned and quantile-residual panels, and a seed
# fixes the randomisation of its quantile residuals:
gfit <- glm(accuracy ~ word_frequency + RT + condition,
            data = lexical_decision, family = binomial)
model_report(gfit, seed = 1)
